title: Relationships
about: Phrasal verbs for friendship and romance: liking someone at once (hit it off, fall for sb, go for a type), flirting and dates (chat sb up, ask sb out), being a couple (go out with sb, pair off), and getting on or falling out with people.

parts.title: Tip: learn from advice columns
parts.note: Фразових дієслів про стосунки — як люди знайомляться, ладнають (get on with each other) і сваряться — дуже багато. Час від часу читай колонки порад у журналах чи онлайн і записуй нові дієслова разом із прийменником і прикладом. Пам'ятай: те саме дієслово в іншому реченні може означати зовсім інше. У таблиці — дієслова цього юніту в іншому поширеному значенні.

rows: go out
Ruth has been going out with Ben since May.
We're going out for a pizza tonight.
fall out
I fell out with my neighbour over his loud music.
One of my teeth fell out when I bit into an apple.
fall for
He fell for her at a friend's party.
Don't fall for that old trick!
fit in
Jo felt she didn't fit in at her new office.
The hairdresser can fit you in at four.
get on
I get on really well with my in-laws.
Get on the bus. It's about to leave!
go for
My brother always goes for girls who love sport.
I think I'll go for the chicken, please.
pair off
On the last night of the trip, everyone seemed to pair off.
The teacher asked us to pair off and practise the dialogue.

items.pattern: go out with sb · often continuous for a period of time: have been going out with sb for a year · about a couple, no with: two people go out (together) · not separable: go out with him, never go him out with · informal
items.meaning: have a romantic relationship with someone you are not married to
items.example: My cousin Anna has been **going out with** a boy from her dance group for six months.
more: We **went out** for three years before we got married.
Is Tom still **going out with** that girl from the bakery?
items.watchOut: «Зустрічатися з кимось» (бути парою) — go out with sb, не meet with sb і не walk with sb (калька з «гуляти з кимось»). Meet sb — просто побачитися. Про пару кажуть без with: They've been going out for a year. Go out без with ще означає «піти кудись розважитися»: We're going out tonight.

items.pattern: fall out (with sb) (over / about sth) · no direct object: the person comes after with · two people fall out · past fell out, fallen out
items.meaning: have an argument with someone, so that you stop being friendly for a while
items.example: Max and his brother **fell out** over who should pay for their mum's birthday present.
more: I **fell out with** my best friend at school, and we didn't speak for a whole term.
It's silly to **fall out** about something as small as where to put the sofa.
items.watchOut: «Посваритися з кимось» — fall out with sb: прийменник with, не on і не to. Причину вводить over або about: fall out over money. Fall out of sth — інше, «випасти»: fall out of bed. Після fall out люди часто миряться (make up); розійтися назовсім — break up.

items.pattern: a chat-up line (noun, informal, British) · use / try a chat-up line (on sb) · a cheesy / terrible / old chat-up line · from the verb chat sb up
items.meaning: something a person says to start a conversation with someone they find attractive, hoping to make that person interested
items.example: 'Haven't we met somewhere before?' must be the oldest **chat-up line** in the world.
more: He tried a cheesy **chat-up line** on my sister, and she burst out laughing.
She thought it was a **chat-up line**, but he really did need directions to the station.
items.watchOut: Іменник пишеться через дефіс: a chat-up line. Дієслово — chat sb up, без дефіса. Американці частіше кажуть a pick-up line.

items.pattern: a falling-out (noun) · have a falling-out (with sb) (over / about sth) · a minor / small / big / serious falling-out · from the verb fall out
items.meaning: an argument that makes people unfriendly towards each other for a while
items.example: We had a small **falling-out** about the washing-up, but we made up before dinner.
more: After their **falling-out**, the two sisters didn't speak for weeks.
Most families have the odd **falling-out** at Christmas.
items.watchOut: Іменник пишеться через дефіс і вживається з артиклем: a falling-out. Не плутай з fallout (одним словом) — «наслідки» або «радіоактивні опади». Кажуть have a falling-out, а не make a falling-out.

items.pattern: fall for sb · not separable: fall for him, never fall him for · past fell for, fallen for · informal · often: fall for each other, fall for sb in a big way
items.meaning: suddenly start to feel very attracted to someone; fall in love with them
items.example: My grandad **fell for** my grandma the first time he saw her dance.
more: I think I'm **falling for** the guy who sells coffee near my office.
They **fell for** each other on a skiing holiday in Austria.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — for: fall for sb, не fall to sb і не fall in sb. Повний варіант — fall in love with sb (тут with). Fall for sth (брехню, трюк) — повестися, купитися: Don't fall for that trick.

items.pattern: fit in (with a group / the team) · fit in at school / at work · no object · past fitted in (UK), fit in (US)
items.meaning: feel comfortable and accepted in a group because you are similar to the other people in it
items.example: It took me a few months to **fit in** at my new school.
more: Our new neighbours **fitted in** straight away. They came to the street party in their first week.
Don't change your whole style just to **fit in with** other people.
items.watchOut: Частку in не пропускай: I didn't fit in (а I didn't fit — це про розмір: «не влазив»). Британською минулий час — fitted in. Fit sb/sth in — інше: знайти час (I can fit you in on Friday).

items.pattern: get along / get on (well) with sb · no object · two people get along / get on · often with well, really well, fine, not very well · get on is more usual in British English
items.meaning: like each other and have a friendly relationship
items.example: My mum and my wife **get along** really well, which makes Christmas much easier.
more: I don't **get on with** my new boss, so I'm looking for another job.
The two boys **got on** fine once they found out they both liked football.
items.watchOut: «Ладнати з кимось» — get along / get on with sb, не get with sb. «Знайти спільну мову» не перекладай дослівно (find a common language): кажуть get on well або hit it off. Well стоїть після дієслова: get on well with sb. How are you getting on? — інше: «Як твої справи?»

items.pattern: ask sb out (for a drink / to dinner / on a date) · the person goes in the middle: ask Emma out, ask her out, never ask out her · passive: be asked out
items.meaning: invite someone to go somewhere with you, like the cinema or a restaurant, because you want to start a romantic relationship
items.example: Josh finally **asked** Emma **out** after months of chatting to her at the bus stop.
more: Why don't you **ask** her **out** for a coffee after class?
My dad **asked** my mum **out** three times before she said yes.
items.watchOut: Займенник — посередині: ask her out, не ask out her. «Запросити на побачення» — ask sb out (on a date), не invite sb on a meeting. Ask sb in / round — запросити зайти до себе додому, це не побачення.

items.pattern: hit it off (with sb) · informal · fixed phrase: always it, never them or each other · past hit it off · two people hit it off / sb hits it off with sb · often: hit it off straight away / immediately
items.meaning: like each other and become friendly as soon as you meet
items.uk: одразу порозумітися, знайти спільну мову з першої зустрічі
items.example: I was nervous about meeting my boyfriend's parents, but his dad and I **hit it off** straight away.
more: Our two dogs **hit it off** in the park, and now they play together every morning.
Did you **hit it off with** your new flatmate?
items.watchOut: It обов'язкове й не змінюється: we hit it off, не we hit off і не we hit each other off. Минулий час — теж hit. Пишеться off (два f), не of. Калька find a common language звучить неприродно — кажуть hit it off або get on well.

items.pattern: pair off (with sb) · no object · usually about people in a group: people start to pair off · also pair sb off (with sb): try to make two people a couple
items.meaning: start a romantic relationship with someone, so that the people in a group become couples
items.example: By our third year at university, most of my friends had **paired off**.
more: Everyone at the summer camp seemed to **pair off** except me.
My aunt keeps trying to **pair** me **off with** her neighbour's son.
items.watchOut: Pair off найчастіше кажуть про групу: усі навколо поступово розбиваються на пари. На уроці pair off / pair up — просто розбитися на пари для вправи, без романтики.

items.pattern: chat sb up · informal, mainly British · with a pronoun, the person goes in the middle: chat her up, never chat up her · with a noun, either order: chat up the waiter / chat the waiter up
items.meaning: talk to someone in a friendly, flirty way because you find them attractive and want them to like you
items.uk: фліртувати з кимось, залицятися, підбивати клинці
items.example: Look at Danny. He's **chatting up** the girl from the ticket office again.
more: A man tried to **chat** me **up** on the train, so I put my headphones on.
Stop **chatting up** the waiter and help me choose a dessert!
items.watchOut: Займенник — посередині: chat her up, не chat up her. Просто «поговорити» — chat (to / with sb), без up: I chatted to my neighbour. З up — це вже флірт. Talk sb up — інше: розхвалювати когось перед іншими.

items.pattern: go for sb/sth (a type of person or thing) · not separable: go for him, never go him for · often with usually / normally / tend to · objects: tall men, blondes, the quiet type, older women, bright colours
items.meaning: be attracted to a particular kind of person, or like a particular kind of thing
items.uk: подобатися (про певний тип людей чи речей)
items.example: I don't usually **go for** men with beards, but Leo is different.
more: My best friend always **goes for** the quiet, serious type.
Lots of teenagers **go for** bright, loud clothes.
items.watchOut: Підмет — той, кому подобається: I go for tall men — «мені подобаються високі чоловіки», а не «високі чоловіки йдуть за мною». Go for має й інші значення: «вибрати» (I'll go for the soup) і «накинутися» (The dog went for the postman), тож дивись на контекст.

warmup.uk: Я зустрічаюся з Максом уже пів року.
warmup.q: I've been ___ Max for six months.
warmup.explain: Зустрічатися (бути парою) — go out with sb. Meet with — мати (ділову) зустріч, walk with — іти пішки поруч.
Посваритися — fall out (with sb) over sth. Break out — спалахнути (про пожежу, війну).

warmup.uk: Здається, я закохалася в нового колегу.
warmup.q: I think I've ___ my new colleague.
warmup.explain: Закохатися в когось — fall for sb або fall in love with sb. Прийменник — for.

warmup.uk: Він досі не запросив мене на побачення.
warmup.explain: Запросити на побачення — ask sb out. Займенник стоїть посередині: ask me out.
Ладнати з кимось — get along / get on (well) with sb. Get together — зустрітися, зібратися; go along with sb — погоджуватися з кимось.

warmup.uk: Ми з нею одразу знайшли спільну мову.
warmup.explain: Одразу сподобатися одне одному — hit it off; it обов'язкове. «Знайти спільну мову» дослівно не перекладають.

warmup.uk: Мені було важко влитися в колектив на новій роботі.
warmup.q: It was hard for me to ___ at my new job.
warmup.explain: Вписатися, стати своїм — fit in (at work, with a group). Fit into потребує додатка й частіше про розмір: fit into a suitcase.

warmup.uk: Якийсь хлопець у барі намагався підбивати до мене клинці.
warmup.q: Some guy at the bar was trying to ___.
warmup.explain: Фліртувати, підбивати клинці — chat sb up. Talk sb up — розхвалювати когось перед іншими.

A.q: My brother and his wife ___ about money now and then, but they always make up.
A.explain: Посваритися — fall out (with sb) about / over sth. Fall away — відпадати, зникати; fall for sb — закохатися.

A.q: Dan is much older than the other students, and he's worried he won't ___.
A.explain: Вписатися в групу — fit in (британською минулий час fitted in). Fit on — про річ, яка налазить зверху (The lid won't fit on), не про людей; fall in — обвалитися (про дах, стелю).

A.q: How long have you been ___ Chris?
A.explain: Бути парою — go out with sb. Date sb — без with: How long have you been dating Chris?

B.q: My neighbour and I ___ the day I moved in. Now we have coffee together every Sunday.
B.explain: Одразу порозумітися — hit it off; без it не можна. Fell out — посварилися, а тут навпаки.

B.q: Why is Ryan standing so close to the new waitress? Is he trying to ___?
B.explain: Фліртувати з кимось — chat sb up, займенник посередині. Talk sb up — розхвалювати когось.

B.q: I don't usually ___ blond men, but Tim is lovely.
B.explain: Подобатися (певний тип) — go for sb/sth: I go for blond men — мені подобаються світловолосі чоловіки.

example.title: The new girl at the dance class
example.uk:
Коли Елла прийшла до нашої п'ятничної групи з танців, вона боялася, що не впишеться. Але ми з нею одразу порозумілися, і невдовзі вона вже ладнала з усіма.

Потім подивитися на нас прийшов мій брат Сем. Зазвичай йому не подобаються тихі дівчата, але він закохався в Еллу, щойно вона всміхнулася. Спершу він спробував познайомитися з нею за допомогою дурнуватої фрази про її туфлі, а вона просто засміялася. Через тиждень він нарешті запросив її на побачення.

Вони зустрічаються вже рік. Одного разу вони трохи посварилися через фільм, але помирилися того ж вечора. Відтоді половина групи розбилася на пари. Я досі сама, але не хвилююся. По п'ятницях у нас тепер новий хлопець.
example.en:
When Ella joined our Friday dance class, she was worried she wouldn't [[fit in|a6]]. But she and I [[hit it off|b1]] straight away, and soon she [[got on|a7]] with everyone.

Then my brother Sam came to watch. He doesn't usually [[go for|b4]] quiet girls, but he [[fell for|a5]] Ella the moment she smiled. First he tried a silly [[chat-up line|a3]] about her shoes, and she just laughed. A week later he finally [[asked her out|a8]].

They've been [[going out|a1]] for a year now. They had one small [[falling-out|a4]] over a film, but they made up the same evening. Since then, half the class has [[paired off|b2]]. I'm still single, but I'm not worried. There's a new guy on Fridays.
